pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 8.2.1 INTENSIVE READING – OGRE STORIES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Intensive reading – Ogre stories

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 8.2.1 Intensive reading – Ogre stories
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How can we read to get specific information from a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify the features of ogre stories for information
2. respond to questions from texts for comprehension
3. use vocabulary related to the theme in sentence construction for comprehension

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 8.2.1 Intensive reading – Ogre stories

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 8.2.1 Intensive reading – Ogre stories

Teach
• Focus skill: identify the features of ogre stories for information.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 8.2.1 Intensive reading – Ogre stories.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 8.2.1 Intensive reading – Ogre stories
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we read to get specific information from a text?
2. How do ogre stories differ from other stories?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
